reason: The cited evidence (E1) reports local chemical fluctuations and enrichment at dislocation cores in a dual-phase HEA, but it does not address CSRO in single-phase FCC equiatomic or subset alloys, nor does it link CSRO to mechanical properties. The key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: CSRO varies systematically among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary/ternary subsets
CSRO can be promoted or suppressed by annealing at 600–800°C followed by rapid quenching
Enhanced CSRO increases local energy barriers for dislocation glide and nucleation
Higher CSRO leads to higher yield strength and altered work hardening, potentially reducing ductility
A quantitative correlation exists between measured CSRO metrics and mechanical properties
